intended: In cases one and three the completion figure was read before the kit was issued: 27 September precedes 4 November at Harlow, and 28 April precedes 5 June at Kelvinside. intended: All four machines are lathes at Bexley on the night shift, so a single change at that plant covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle" and that "every machine here drew from that supply", so the new lubricant reached the bearings in all four cases. A higher-grade lubricant extends bearing life on its own, and every machine is compared against its own previous cycle - run before the switch - rather than against a machine on the same lubricant over the same period. Nothing in the log separates the redesigned bearing from the change of grade.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." Better lubricant plainly extends bearing life, so the 260-410 extra hours on all four Bexley lathes cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the purchase counts over the sessions that signed in, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each segment never signed in. The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases for the segment, so the numbers describe three quarters of the population the claim is about. Signed-in shoppers arrive with saved cards and addresses and convert at different rates from guests, so the uncounted quarter cannot be assumed to have moved with the counted part. The four segments span four devices, four countries, four months and four traffic sources, and the sign-in gap is stated per segment, so the same three-quarters coverage sits in every case rather than being filled by any of them.
reported: The purchase counts 'cover the sessions that signed in, and a quarter of each segment never signed in', so the 4-7 percent lift is measured on a narrower population (signed-in sessions) than the claim about purchases on the checkout page as a whole; a shift in who signs in would produce the same numbers.

reported: The purchase counts "cover the sessions that signed in" while "a quarter of each segment never signed in," so the 4-7 percent gains are measured on a subset that excludes a quarter of sessions, not on purchases generally as the claim asserts. (The price clause is neutralized - prices matched the earlier period "to the nearest cent" - so the coverage gap is the live problem.)

intended: The mid-passage line states that figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and that about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout. The revenue-per-order numbers are therefore tallied over roughly four fifths of the orders on each line, while the claim is about revenue per order on the repriced lines as a whole, self-checkout baskets included. Self-checkout baskets are a systematically different set of purchases from staffed-till baskets, typically smaller and quicker, so the 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent gains recorded on the staffed-till subset are consistent with revenue per order across all orders holding flat or falling. The four lines sit at Harlow Street, Pell Basin, Ordway Quay and Tamsin Row across four different months, and the same fifth is missing at each of them, so spreading the cases over stores, categories and months does nothing to close the gap.
reported: The numbers cover a narrower population than the claim: 'Figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout.' Roughly 20 percent of orders are excluded from the revenue-per-order figures, and self-checkout baskets differ systematically, so a 4-7 percent rise on staffed-till orders does not establish revenue per order rose overall.

intended: In cases one and three the attack counts were recorded before the inhaler was started: 28 February precedes 4 March at Harrowfield, and 30 August precedes 5 September at Calderbank. Half the evidence therefore describes a reduction that had already happened when treatment began, so it cannot be evidence for the inhaler. The two remaining cases, Brightmoor and Dunmorrow, are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the inhaler was started: case one "started 4 March, had 6 fewer attacks by 28 February" and case three "started 5 September, had 7 fewer attacks by 30 August." The improvement window closes before the intervention begins, so those cases cannot be effects of the inhaler.
